name: BMW S70/2 6.1 L V12 (McLaren F1, 1993-1998)
summary: A 60-degree, 48-valve V12 with twelve individual throttles breathing from a carbon airbox just above the driver's head; even 60-degree firing gives the classic smooth V12 howl, with unusually loud induction noise.

firing_order.note: Not found for the S70/2. motor-car.net gives 1-7-5-11-3-9-6-12-2-8-4-10 for the related two-valve BMW M70 V12 (https://www.motor-car.net/bmw-engines/item/16057-m70-engine); the S70/2 shares its layout and bore spacing but is a different engine, so this is a lead, not a sourced value. Cylinder numbering by bank not found.

crank.note: Not described on any page opened. A 60-degree V12 normally has six shared crank pins at 120 degrees; not sourced for this engine.

firing_intervals_deg.note: Not stated on any page opened. A 60-degree V12 with shared pins fires evenly every 60 degrees; this is general engine knowledge, not a sourced value for the S70/2.

valves_per_cylinder.note: Chain-driven DOHC per bank with continuously variable inlet valve timing (VANOS-type phasing of the inlet cam). Heads based on the BMW S50 six (Wikipedia says S50B30, unixnerd says S50B32).

redline_rpm.note: Wikipedia: 'The engine's rev limiter is set at 7,500 rpm.'

peak_power_rpm.note: McLaren's specification sheet says 7,500 rpm; Wikipedia's McLaren F1 and BMW M70 pages say 7,400 rpm.

peak_torque_nm.note: 480 lb-ft. Wikipedia's McLaren F1 page says 650 N·m.

peak_torque_rpm.note: Wikipedia's BMW M70 table says 6,700 rpm, which disagrees with McLaren's own sheet and with its McLaren F1 page.

intake_type.value: individual throttles: 12 single throttle valves, carbon composite airbox; no variable intake geometry; two injectors per cylinder (one near the valve for low rpm, one higher in the tract for high rpm)
intake_type.note: Throttles and airbox from McLaren's sheet; injectors and the rejected variable geometry from Wikipedia.

exhaust_notes.value: Four Inconel catalysts with individual lambda control.

missing: crank layout as a sourced statement

sources.what: McLaren Automotive specification sheet 'McLaren F1 GT Roadcar', powertrain type S 70/2 (third-party host). Manufacturer; the GT uses the standard road-car engine.
English Wikipedia McLaren F1 page; rev limit, injection, catalysts.
English Wikipedia BMW M70 page, S70/2 section and version table.
unixnerd.co.uk BMW V12 page; enthusiast site, used only for the head-origin disagreement.
motor-car.net BMW M70 page; firing order of the M70, not the S70/2.

name.note: McLaren Automotive "McLaren F1 Road Car - Specification"; standard road car, not the GT or LM. The S70/2 of this def.

curb_kg.note: Quote: "Kerb Weight 1140 / 2513 kg / lbs". Convention not stated; Wikipedia (lead) calls 1,140 kg dry and gives 1,260 kg kerb, unverified; Autocar's 1994 test (paywalled, not read) is said to give 1,138 kg with half a tank.

gears.note: Quote: "1st Gear Ratio 3.23/8.7 ... 2nd 2.19/12.7, 3rd 1.71/16.7, 4th 1.39/20.0, 5th 1.16/24.0, 6th Gear Ratio 0.93/30.0". The second number reads as mph per 1,000 rpm (inference).

final_drive.note: DERIVED (ours). Published: "Final Drive Ratio 2.37:1", "Transverse unit with high speed bevel gears and spur final drive". With 2.37, 6th would give 38.0 mph per 1,000 rpm on this tyre against the sheet's 30.0; the shortfall is the same factor (about 1.24-1.27) in all six gears. Solving each gear's mph/1000 for the overall ratio with a 0.350 m rolling radius gives 2.87-2.95 (mean 2.93). Car and Driver 1994, via Wikipedia (not read): 221 mph at 7,500 rpm in 6th, i.e. 29.5 mph/1000, agreeing with the sheet.

wheel_radius_m.note: Estimated (ours): rolling radius taken as 98% of the unloaded radius computed from the tyre size (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio).

top_speed_kmh.note: Quote: "Top Speed 386/240.1 km/h / mph". This is the 1998 Ehra-Lessien record run with the rev limiter raised to 8,300 rpm (Wikipedia, lead: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_F1).

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'McLaren F1' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: Rear mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive.
